variations.oneLine: The current perched raven redrawn with raven anatomy (flat crown, hooked bill, nape, wedge tail) plus a separate head-and-bill drawing for 16-22 px.
variations.bestFor: Drop-in successor on every surface that carries raven.svg today: launcher, taskbar, README, installer, favicon >= 32; tray and favicon-16 via the -16 head; ic_stat via -status.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Reads as a raven from 32 px up' and is a path-data swap in the same 108 box and translate(2,11), launcher safe circle held at 32.4 dp (current 32.6).
variations.topWeakness: README: the full mark at 16 px 'is still a smudge with a bill' so a second drawing must be maintained; vs mark-02 it is 'a tone decision, not a quality one', i.e. the least visibly new mark.

variations.oneLine: The same raven cut from 12 straight edges with a round eye; ships a SMIL unfold build-in, a 28x7 braille tracing and a 9-edge head for 16 px.
variations.bestFor: Anything rasterised by third parties at unknown sizes (.ico, store listing) and anything redrawn in code, ASCII or animation; splash build-in via -unfold.svg.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Different from mark-01 at icon size, not only at hero size'; 12 vertices 'port, morph and trace trivially' and the morph and braille claims 'now ship their proof'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'hard edges want some geometry in the surrounding type and icon system or they date next to soft Material 3 surfaces'; at 512 'some will read it as a stealth shape before a bird'.

variations.oneLine: The raven as a Lucide-style 24-grid 2 px stroke icon with a filled companion for <= 20 px, shown in a set beside Lucide-equivalents.
variations.bestFor: In-app icon sets, menu rows, tray menu, README badges, anything tinted with currentColor at the weight of neighbouring icons.
variations.topStrength: README: correct Lucide construction at the same optical weight as its neighbours; honest switch point 'stroke at >= 24, filled at <= 20, stated and shown'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'Not the canonical brand mark, not the launcher icon'; the filled companion 'is a fat bird' and the tile 'is a blob at 512 px'.

variations.oneLine: A 16x16 master and its 32x32 twin in grid.txt generate the vector marks, half-block / braille / 7-bit terminal art, blink and call frames and per-density PNGs from the same cells.
variations.bestFor: A terminal-native identity where tray icon, CLI help raven and tmux banner are literally the same drawing; tray at 16/32, Android adaptive foreground, .ico, the only CLI-safe raven form.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Cohesion across surfaces is structural, not stylistic'; pixel-exact at 16 and 32, every Android density and every .ico size; 'the only direction in the set that ships a CLI-safe 7-bit raven'.
variations.topWeakness: README: the integer-scale rule - at 125/150 % trays (20/24 px) 'ragged (scaled) or small (padded)', the 10 %-inset tile 'is never exact at 48 or 256'; 'Chunky above 64 px by design; next to the smooth current mark it reads retro'.

variations.oneLine: A raven head and breast cut as negative space out of a solid rounded square (also a circle and a terminal window), eye as a pixel-aligned ink cell, one evenodd path.
variations.bestFor: System tray, notification icon and favicon tinted by state; app icon via -tile from 48 px up; avatars via -circle; docs/CLI chrome via -window.
variations.topStrength: README: 'the one shape that is genuinely safe at 16px in a tray, and it still carries a bird'; the inverse 'is the best single image in the set'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'It is a head, not a whole raven' - at hero size 'it reads corvid (crow, rook) before raven; it needs the full mark (or mark-06-flight) beside it'; tile is soft at 32, use the untiled primary below 48.

variations.oneLine: The raven in flight from below with fingered primaries and a wedge tail, for hero, splash and installer, plus a three-shape 24x24 'bird returning' glyph for the tray's attention state.
variations.bestFor: README hero, splash/launch moment and installer welcome panel (the 192x108 splash lockup); the small glyph as a tray/notification attention cue at 16-32.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Says raven more specifically than any profile mark can' (wedge tail and fingered primaries) and 'carries the brand story literally'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'this cannot replace the primary mark; it is a companion'; the full mark at 16 is 'a dark T-shaped smudge' and the small glyph 'is not a raven... at 512 it is a dove, a swallow or a sword'.

variations.oneLine: The canonical raven at 48 columns in half-block and braille (hand-tuned), plus an 80-column shaded poster kept in extras/.
variations.bestFor: Server-side poster: installer console page, docs, a huginn-status --banner, the opening frame of a terminal animation; needs >= 48 columns and 15 rows.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Reads as the raven, not as some bird, in both alphabets'; half-block 'needs nothing from the font but the three block glyphs' and is space-padded.
variations.topWeakness: README: '15 rows is taller than most splash budgets'; braille is font-dependent and block art stripes on GitHub's 1.45 line-height.

variations.oneLine: The raven at 24x8, the splash / README size, half-block redrawn pixel by pixel and braille hand-tuned.
variations.bestFor: Server-side splash after attach, installer console, the README hero written as text (lockup-d), Termux welcome, first frame of an animation.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Reads as the raven at a 16px cell: bill, eye, throat, tail all there' in 8 rows, so it 'survives a 24-row terminal with a wordmark and a prompt'.
variations.topWeakness: README: the one-pixel eye 'can vanish into the gap' on font-drawn blocks, half-block stripes on GitHub, and 'hand-tuning does not transfer automatically: a new mark means a new src/half-24.grid'.

variations.oneLine: Hand-drawn 1-, 2-, 3-, 4- and 5-line ravens in Unicode and ASCII; the one-row glyph is the four-cell wedge/body/head/bill monogram and the ASCII one is (o)=-.
variations.bestFor: tmux status-left, the server's first line, the --help header (raven-4line-ascii-a is a drop-in for huginn.sh:988), TUI headers, ravens beside wordmarks.
variations.topStrength: README: 'From 2 lines up every size has a candidate that reads as a bird at 16px without a caption'; 'every client-facing size has a 7-bit twin'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'The 1-line glyphs are not ravens'; the leading glyph is a geometric-shape character 'whose size differs per font' (and type-system.md measures it absent from JetBrains Mono and IBM Plex Mono).

variations.oneLine: Raven + figlet HUGINN in four faces, the first-line banners (Unicode and ASCII), the --help header and a tmux status-left segment with a needs-you condition.
variations.bestFor: Server splash on 80 columns (lockup-a), README hero as a code block (lockup-d), CLI help heredoc (help-header-ascii), tmux status bar (snippet).
variations.topStrength: README: 'the client files finally have something that is theirs (e, the help header, the ASCII banner)'; lockup.py 'recomposes from any raven file and any figlet font'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'A stock figlet face is still a stock figlet face'; the tmux snippet puts 'Gold ground only while Claude needs you', which contradicts the colour dimension's gold = working rule.

variations.oneLine: Runes as bullets or separators: verdict no; plus the state glyph table (filled circle / triangle / hollow circle / dot, narrow twins, ASCII * ! o -) that replaces the emoji tab-title icons.
variations.bestFor: Brand-book rule 'runes are out of terminal output'; tab-title, huginn-status and Telegram state glyphs; bullets and separators for terminal output.
variations.topStrength: README: a rendering-based verdict backed by fc-list ('no common monospace font has the Runic block'); the state glyphs 'are in every monospace font'.
variations.topWeakness: The table disagrees with the colour dimension (diamond, not triangle, for attention) and anim-05-status (ASCII - for waiting); ambiguous East Asian width can make the glyphs two cells in CJK locales.

variations.oneLine: The baseline: today's figlet ansi_shadow block capitals with a double-line box-drawing shadow, 49x6.
variations.bestFor: Control only; still the heaviest server-side banner if nothing else is adopted.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Heaviest and most legible mark in the set; reads at 12 px on both grounds in every face... including Liberation Mono'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'Generic: this is the default banner of ten thousand projects'; the shadow 'fights the flat, monochrome-first rule'.

variations.oneLine: Lighter block capitals in the three universal block glyphs, 40x5, with a real diagonal N.
variations.bestFor: README hero rendered to an image, server banners, installer console; the caps half of a block-only system with word-03 and word-06.
variations.topStrength: README: uses only the three block glyphs 'which every monospace font has (Liberation Mono row in the preview renders it completely)'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'Still a stock figlet font; distinctive only by restraint'; half-block seams in GitHub pre.

variations.oneLine: Lowercase block 'huginn' in the same bitmap face plus the brand cursor column, 43x7.
variations.bestFor: Server-side attach banner, huginn-status, the terminal twin of type-02-plex-mono; the cursor is an animation hook.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Lowercase and quiet; looks like a command, not a logo'; renders completely in Liberation Mono.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'Seven rows is tall for a phone splash; the word plus a prompt line eats a third of a 24-row screen'; the cursor column is mandatory in every placement.

variations.oneLine: A 3-row heavy box-drawing narrow HUGINN, 16x3, with the N hand-fixed.
variations.bestFor: Narrow phone terminals (Termux after attach, huginn-status on a phone) where heavy box glyphs exist.
variations.topStrength: README: '16 columns: fits anywhere, including a 40-column session with room for a prompt beside it'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'Heavy box glyphs and the diagonal are absent from Liberation Mono (the preview's Liberation row is all tofu)'; no 7-bit twin; word-06 took the narrow slot in the verdict.

variations.oneLine: A 3-row half-block narrow HUGINN, 23x3, using only full and upper-half blocks.
variations.bestFor: The sub-34-column mark (the verdict's choice): narrow phone terminals, installer console at small sizes, a tmux pane on a phone.
variations.topStrength: README: 'The most font-independent mark in the set: two glyphs, both universal; the only narrow mark that renders in Liberation Mono'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'The N is a square arch... the last two letters can scan as pi pi'; 'it says 8-bit more than modern'.

variations.oneLine: Hand-fixed slim 7-bit ASCII capitals, 40x3, seam-free everywhere.
variations.bestFor: CLI --help masthead, release notes, email, NOTICE files; README where block seams must be avoided.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Renders identically everywhere: terminal, GitHub pre, plain text; nothing can be missing from a font'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'Thin... the underscores render as dashed lines in every font'; 'next to the heavy marks it looks like a different brand'; dropped from the type-system verdict.

variations.oneLine: The italic: figlet slant lowercase 'huginn' with the upright cursor, Unicode and a 7-bit ascii.txt twin, 36x6.
variations.bestFor: CLI sign-offs after attach or update, the installer's final page, README section dividers.
variations.topStrength: README: 'The only italic/script candidate that reads cleanly at terminal size'; ascii.txt is pure 7-bit and safe in a PowerShell here-string.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'A slanted figlet font is a nostalgic idiom; it reads 1990s BBS before it reads modern'.

variations.oneLine: Hand-drawn thin box-drawing HUGINN with a true diagonal N, 33x5, in rounded, square and ASCII charsets.
variations.bestFor: Server-side splash in desktop terminals, installer console, the CLI help masthead via ascii.txt; the base of word-10-perch.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Designed letterforms... nothing in the figlet corpus looks like this'; 'the three charsets degrade gracefully'.
variations.topWeakness: README: the rounded file depends on glyphs 'Liberation Mono does not have'; JetBrains Mono notches the diagonal; 'Hairlines are the lightest thing on a dark phone screen'.

variations.oneLine: The hairline letters with the raven (rasterised from raven.svg onto a 14x10 half-block grid) standing in for the I; three charsets plus a geometry SVG pair.
variations.bestFor: The server-side signature banner (huginn-status, attach banner, installer console), CLI masthead via ascii.txt, README hero and docs via the SVGs, the apps' About line.
variations.topStrength: README: 'A real lockup, not a font: the raven is primary, in the one place it had no presence (the terminal)'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'The word is still HUG [bird] NN' with seven blank cells on row 1; the bird is a rasterisation of the current raven.svg and must be redone for a new mark; the ASCII bird is 'textured, not solid'.

variations.oneLine: The one-row mark (o> with state variants (-> and (!>, 3 cells, 7-bit.
variations.bestFor: tmux status bar, terminal tab titles, CLI version and update lines, log prefixes.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Three cells, 7-bit, identical in every font and every terminal; nothing can be missing'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'A generic bird, not a raven'; competes with ascii-03's one-row pick that three other dimensions already adopted.

variations.oneLine: Schibsted Grotesk 800 wordmark and UI family plus JetBrains Mono, with outlined wordmark.svg / lockup.svg and dark twins; the type-system.md verdict.
variations.bestFor: The product type system (Android, Compose desktop, docs), README hero and installer as SVG, About screen, social cards.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Holds up at 24 px (notification, tray tooltip)'; one family for the UI; 'The README hero no longer needs a font or a pre: the SVGs exist'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'A grotesk is the safe choice; nothing about the letterforms says raven'; the lockups use the current raven.svg only; tittle lockup untested below 44 px.

variations.oneLine: IBM Plex Mono-led identity: lowercase 'huginn' typed with the raven as the cursor; Plex Sans for titles and body.
variations.bestFor: CLI-adjacent surfaces (installer, README, docs code headers, tray tooltip); app UI 'if the owner wants the phone to feel like the terminal it mirrors'.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Only direction where wordmark, UI and terminal are literally one face'; box 128/128 and blocks 32/32 so every block wordmark renders in-app.
variations.topWeakness: README: Theme.kt's intent is 'a terminal that does not look like a terminal emulator; a mono-led UI pulls the other way'; 'The tittle lockup does not work in this direction at any size tested'; Plex has 1/96 geometric shapes.

variations.oneLine: Instrument Serif display wordmark with a carved edge, Instrument Sans UI, JetBrains Mono code; the serif never below 28 px.
variations.bestFor: Hero surfaces only: README masthead as SVG, docs masthead, social cards, installer wizard, About box, release notes.
variations.topStrength: README: 'The most distinctive and the most premium of the three; the only one where the letterforms themselves carry a hint of the carved/Nordic motif'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'Weak at small sizes: the 24 px serif wordmark is thin and loses the serifs on a phone'; Regular and Italic only; no outlined SVG was produced.

variations.oneLine: Two one-line 'connecting' spinners: (a) a 3-cell wingbeat at 2 Hz and (b) a thought leaving the one-row raven for the host ring and returning, each with a 7-bit twin.
variations.bestFor: CLI/Termux while ssh or tmux attach negotiates (7-bit twins); huginn-status and the README (Unicode).
variations.topStrength: README: (b) 'tells the product story and has the arrived frame a progress indicator needs'; both 'ship a 7-bit twin that can be pasted into the client today'.
variations.topWeakness: README: (a) 'is faster than [the house pulse] on purpose'; the glyph raven 'is a bird by convention' and the 7-bit (o> 'is a beak and an eye, no more'.

variations.oneLine: 3- and 5-row perched ravens that flap-hop, a landing for connected and a takeoff for detached, with 7-bit twins grown from the client's help-screen raven.
variations.bestFor: CLI attach and detach moments and polling (7-bit); huginn status on the host (Unicode); README GIF.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Landing and takeoff give connected and detached a visual verb that is the brand story'; 'the help raven is no longer a dead end but the resting pose of an animation'.
variations.topWeakness: README: the wings-down pose 'is a downward arrowhead in a still' and the turn 'is still a hard cut'; the 7-bit landing ends on today's (o)==- raven, which ascii-03 proposes to replace.

variations.oneLine: The 20- and 24-column ravens (sampled from raven.svg) idling: a blink and a head tuck with multi-second holds.
variations.bestFor: huginn status on the host above its output (20 col); the README GIF (24 col).
variations.topStrength: README: 'Faithful to the mark at 13 px cells: eye, beak, back, tail notch all present'; the holds make it 'calm everywhere'.
variations.topWeakness: README: Unicode only, 'no 7-bit twin of a 20-column raven worth shipping'; 'the body is a slab at this size' and a new mark means resampling.

variations.oneLine: Splash: a braille glyph rain assembles the 24-column raven crown-first, the tagline types in, 1.5 s at 24 fps or 1.6 s at 12 fps; a dissolve for exit; a 42x8 7-bit boot for the client.
variations.bestFor: README hero GIF; the client's first run (Unicode boot from a ~/.huginn/boot.frames data file, else the inline 7-bit boot).
variations.topStrength: README: 'Under 2 s, and the rain reads as rain'; deterministic; the bash player 'plays the 36 frames in 1573 ms under a pty' with no per-frame fork.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'Dense: 36 frames of 42x17 is 64 KB... it has to be a data file, and the update path for that file is specified, not written'; '24 fps on Termux is unmeasured'.

variations.oneLine: A tmux status segment at 1 fps: a thought drifts (working), a four-step breathe, the raven turns to face you with a diamond marker (needs you), still (waiting); plus the state-to-frame-to-colour table.
variations.bestFor: server/tmux.conf status bar on the host; the table maps every state vocabulary the product uses.
variations.topStrength: README: '1-fps-safe: every frame is a complete, sensible status on its own'; 'One glyph, shared with anim-01, so the brand has one 1-row raven'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'A segment that changes every second can be distracting'; the attention colour depends on an open colour decision; huginn-status-frame is a sketch.

variations.oneLine: The eye blinks: an oversize ink lid closes over the evenodd hole for 320 ms on an irregular 12 s cadence; otherwise the mark is still.
variations.bestFor: App idle state (empty-session screen, connection card), README hero as an SVG img, any mark shown at 48 px or more.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Zero new geometry: the mark is path#raven referenced once'; the resting state is the mark; poster.png, fallback.gif and an AVD sketch ship.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'Below about 48 px the eye is a 1-2 px hole and the blink is invisible'; prefers-reduced-motion is 'NOT honoured' inside img (Chromium only tested).

variations.oneLine: 93 terminal glyphs (blocks baked as rects, 14 shade glyphs as text) fly in and settle into the silhouette, then the solid mark takes over, 2.0 s.
variations.bestFor: App splash (re-implemented natively in Compose) and the docs hero inline; glyphs.txt as a README block.
variations.topStrength: README: 'The one piece that fuses the owner's ASCII ask with the mark: terminal glyphs become the raven'; the resting state is exactly the static mark at every size.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'At 64 px and below the scatter reads as noise; the piece needs 160 px or more'; the CLI-banner use was withdrawn; the same idea exists as anim-ascii anim-04-boot and as mark-04-pixel.

variations.oneLine: The perched raven crouches, unfurls, lifts into a flight silhouette, exits right, returns from the left and perches: a 5 s loop with a 2 s hold, in-app only.
variations.bestFor: Desktop 'reconnecting' state (cut at the next landing), first-run or installer finish page.
variations.topStrength: README: 'The one animation that tells the brand story rather than decorating the mark'; wings are continuous across both hand-overs.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'The flight silhouette is NEW geometry... a redrawn mark needs its flyer redrawn'; body swaps are cuts; README-hero use withdrawn until img reduced-motion is verified.

variations.oneLine: Tray IDLE to ATTENTION: the raven slides to its badge layout in 300 ms, the badge pops, a ring leaves the raven twice, then rest; a 64 px sprite at 10 fps with a Java2D spec and generated frame tables.
variations.bestFor: Desktop tray transition into ATTENTION (TrayIcons.kt); the same frames as a needs-you badge on the desktop session list.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Starts and ends on frames the tray already draws; the Kotlin change is additive'; the slide replaces today's hard snap.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'this animation does not fix the mark's small-size problem, it works around it with the badge'; 'A ring is a generic notification idiom'; three other proposals exist for the same tray cue.

variations.oneLine: Three 'Claude is working' indicators: (a) a falling feather, (b) an eye scan, (c) a block cursor breathing on the apps' stepped PulseDot clock; recommendation (c).
variations.bestFor: Chat UI on phone and desktop next to the streaming message; an AVD sketch for widget or notification surfaces.
variations.topStrength: README: (c) 'reads at 16 px, zero new geometry, terminal-native, one rhythm across the app'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'a block cursor is a cliche; a stepped breath at 6 fps is visibly stepped at hero size'; (a) and (b) are hero-only; the cursor height must follow the chosen mark.

variations.oneLine: The current palette finished: five surface tiers, three outline tiers, a brand-native state ladder (stone / gold / lit gold), slot-pinned ANSI-16, tmux, VHS and CLI tables; nothing shipped moves.
variations.bestFor: The default direction for app, tray, README, demo and CLI; Theme.kt becomes a rename plus new tokens; the migration list names every file.
variations.topStrength: README: 'Zero brand drift: ground, ink, accent, inkMark, boneTile, error and secondary are today's values'; every pair proven AA in contrast.txt.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'warn and attention share the brightYellow slot... the same hue, 17 L* apart'; 'It is the least new'; light-scheme stateAttention 'is a very dark umber'.

variations.oneLine: A cool slate ground with bone ink, one verdigris accent in the cyan slot over a bronze secondary; the direction where the overhaul is visible in colour.
variations.bestFor: The whole product if the owner wants the change seen; strongest on the desktop app and in the terminal.
variations.topStrength: README: 'The cleanest terminal semantics: the accent (cyan) and warning (brightYellow) are different hues, 128 degrees apart'; 'the best raven story in the palette itself'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'Furthest from what ships: every surface, inkMark and boneTile move'; 'It borders on the dark-dev-tool convention'; the 16-colour CLI accent is brightCyan, not the exact accent.

variations.oneLine: A soot ground, warm bone ink and one ember accent (oxblood in daylight) with olive, ash and cream-amber around it.
variations.bestFor: Desktop app, installer and README hero 'where one hot accent on dark has room to be dramatic'; the README says it is less suited to Android notification and permission surfaces.
variations.topStrength: README: 'The most distinctive and the most brand of the three: unmistakably the raven's eye in firelight'.
variations.topWeakness: README: 'Main risk: the ember is Claude's colour' (terracotta-on-dark); 'Orange is a warning colour in every OS'; the ember has no ANSI slot and error 'can never be a pure red here'.

variations.oneLine: Shared layer, not a candidate: the ANSI-16 rules, slot pins, 16-colour state ladder, the one-row raven and install notes common to the three directions, with the three terminal mocks on one sheet.
variations.bestFor: Understanding what carries over whichever hue wins: CLI colour tables, tmux snippet, VHS theme, Ansi.kt palette, Windows Terminal scheme.
variations.topStrength: color/README: 'the state system, the tiers, the slot pins, the terminal layer and the one-row raven carry over unchanged - they are the deliverable; the hue is the choice'.
variations.topWeakness: color/README 'Not done': no light-scheme terminal palette; cli-colors.ps1 'is syntax-reviewed by eye... there is no pwsh in the build container to execute it'.

gaps.what: No cross-dimension composite exists on any candidate mark: every wordmark lockup (type-01 lockup.svg, word-10's bird), every ascii file, every anim-vector file and the colour sheets are built on the current raven.svg; the only new-mark composites are marks-b/system.png (its own three marks) and mark-04's own art. The owner cannot see mark-01/02 in a lockup, a terminal splash, a tray sheet in the chosen palette or a blink.
gaps.why it matters: The ask is a cohesive system across platforms; the decision is a system, not a part, and today nothing shows one assembled. ascii/README ('The owner will re-run regen.sh on the chosen new mark'), anim-vector/README ('run bash build.sh') and type-01 ('regenerate the same way') all defer it.
gaps.which dimension: cross: marks-a, marks-b, wordmark, ascii, anim-vector, color

gaps.what: Installer composition: the brief lists packaging/wizard.bmp; color gives two token names, type-system says use type-01 wordmark.svg/lockup.svg, mark-06 offers a 192x108 splash lockup, but no wizard.bmp mock at the NSIS bitmap's real size exists in any direction.
gaps.why it matters: The installer is a named surface and the first thing a Windows user sees; three dimensions each supply a part and none composes it.

gaps.what: Android notification, lock-screen permission prompt and Glance widgets: only marks-b/system.png sketches a notification row; no shade mock with the -status silhouettes plus the notification accent (color migration: 'where the notification builder sets an accent, it takes primary'), no expanded or large-icon view, and no widget mock although the brief lists bare GlanceTheme as off-brand.
gaps.why it matters: The Android app and 'permission prompts answered from the lock screen' are core surfaces in the brief; they are covered by one table row each.

gaps.what: Linux desktop notifications: color's migration says LibnotifyNotifier takes '--icon=<path to the brand raven PNG> for both' but no mark ships a PNG at libnotify sizes (mark-04 ships tray PNGs only).
gaps.why it matters: A claim in the migration list with no artefact behind it; the stock dialog-* icons stay until someone renders one.

gaps.what: README section headers still use emoji (brief's off-brand list) and no variation proposes the replacement; ascii-05 gives terminal bullets and state glyphs, nothing addresses Markdown headers or badge colours (color: 'badges may take the accent hex (optional)').
gaps.why it matters: The README is the first brand surface most people see; the hero is covered five ways and the rest of the page not at all.

gaps.what: The terminal title and state glyph set is proposed four times (ascii-05, color state mapping, anim-05-status, word-11 states.txt) with differing glyphs and no single resolved table and no huginn-claude-title patch; the brief says 'A unified semantic set must map onto all of these'.
gaps.why it matters: Every dimension assumes the others own it; the brand book needs one table.
gaps.which dimension: color (owner of the semantic set), ascii

gaps.what: Nothing was verified on a real terminal or device: ascii/README 'nothing was looked at in a real terminal emulator on a real device'; anim-ascii ps-player.ps1 'Not run here'; color cli-colors.ps1 'syntax-reviewed by eye'; anim-04-boot '24 fps on Termux is unmeasured'; anim-vector tested in Chromium only (Firefox, Safari, GitHub camo and img reduced-motion open); AVD sketches 'not compiled'; mark-04 half-block seams in real emulators 'not verified'.
gaps.why it matters: PowerShell, Termux and the README are named platforms; the CLI pieces of every bundle rest on fallbacks that have only been reasoned about.

gaps.what: Motion claimed without an artefact: word-10 'the bird leaves the I and returns'; word-03 'the cursor blinks or the raven replaces it'; type-02 'cheap to animate (blink the raven, or let it fly off and return)'; mark-05 'the hole can also fill from the bottom as a progress or session attaching motion' and the eye-cell blink; mark-06 'wings from folded to spread... and a settle into the perched mark' (anim-03 does a version on the current mark with its own flyer); mark-02's unfold 'starts from a hairline... a build-in that starts from the eye or from nothing is a one-line change, not done here'.
gaps.why it matters: The owner asked for animation; several marks sell themselves on motion that only the READMEs describe.

gaps.what: No splash or launch-screen composition at phone or desktop proportions and no About panel mock, although mark-06, mark-05-window, anim-02-assemble and anim-03 all name the splash as their surface; anim-02 says Compose 'is best re-implemented natively'.
gaps.why it matters: The splash is the one moment where mark, wordmark, palette and motion meet; it is named by four variations and drawn by none.

gaps.what: Server-side wiring is unwritten: anim-04-boot's boot.frames update path 'specified, not written'; anim-05's huginn-status-frame 'a sketch'; ascii-04's @huginn_state tmux option 'needs one line added to huginn-claude-title'; no patch for huginn-claude-title's HUGINN_ICON_* defaults.
gaps.why it matters: The tmux and title surfaces are where the CLI identity lives; without the hooks the frames and snippets cannot be tried.

gaps.what: Favicon / .ico / docs-site header: mark-04 lists .ico sizes and the other marks say 'favicon-16: the -16 drawing', but no .ico or favicon set is produced and no docs header mock uses the typographic lockup.
gaps.why it matters: The web surfaces are implied by the README hero and type-01's docs-site use.

gaps.what: Muninn: the brief says 'a second raven form may be reserved for' the memory companion and the README has a 'Memory (the other raven)' section; no variation reserves or tests a companion form (mark-06 is Huginn's own flight).
gaps.why it matters: If a second form is wanted later it should be chosen with the first, not against it.

gaps.what: The demo GIF: each colour direction ships the VHS theme line, and anim-04-boot says the hero GIF 'should be recorded with VHS on the chosen terminal theme', but no demo is re-recorded with the new banner, spinner or theme.
gaps.why it matters: The brief lists the Catppuccin demo as an incoherence; the fix is specified but not shown.

gaps.what: Acknowledged omissions: no light-scheme terminal palette (color 'Not done'); no outlined SVG for type-02 or type-03 ('only the recommended one got that work'); no 7-bit twin of the medium idle raven (anim-03); no hand-pass in a vector editor on mark-01's curves (marks-a 'Not done here').
gaps.why it matters: Each is stated honestly; listed so the brand book does not assume them.

conflicts.what: The one-row raven for tmux status-left, the first line and tab titles: ascii-03 picks the four-cell wedge/body/head/bill glyph with the block-only fallback and ASCII (o)=- (5 cells); anim-01, anim-05 and all three colour terminal layers adopt that glyph but the colour cli-colors use today's 6-cell (o)==- as the 7-bit form; word-11-oneline proposes (o> (3 cells) for the same slots and anim-ascii names (o> as its font fallback; mark-04 says 'a status line should carry a state dot or the ASCII eye-and-bill (o)>'. Four ASCII one-row birds and two Unicode ones for one slot. type-system.md adds that JetBrains Mono (the recommended bundled mono) lacks the leading geometric-shape glyph, so the ascii-03 pick falls to a fallback font inside the apps' terminal view.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: One Unicode one-row glyph and one 7-bit one-row glyph, and whether the in-app terminal view may show the geometric-shape glyph at all.

conflicts.what: The tab-title / status glyph table: ascii-05 uses filled circle / triangle / hollow circle / dot (ASCII * ! o -); the colour state mapping uses filled circle / diamond / hollow circle / small hollow circle (ASCII * ! o -); anim-05-status uses filled circle / diamond / hollow circle with ASCII * ! - (waiting = dash); word-11 uses (o> (-> (!>. Attention is a triangle or a diamond, waiting's ASCII is o or -.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: One table, owned by the colour dimension (which owns the semantic set), adopted verbatim by ascii-05, anim-05 and huginn-claude-title.

conflicts.what: What gold means in the tmux bar: ascii-04's snippet and preview-mocks put the glyph in rune-gold while idle and 'Gold ground only while Claude needs you'; color-01 and anim-05 say 'gold means working, as it does in the apps', idle takes stateIdle and attention takes the lit gold #F3D58F. ascii-04's tmux-status-left is the only one of the three tmux implementations with the inverted rule.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: Adopt the colour ladder (idle muted, working accent, attention lit accent) and re-cut ascii-04's snippet and mock, or keep gold as the attention tint.

conflicts.what: Attention colour: the apps today map attention to error red; every colour direction introduces stateAttention as the accent lit up (#F3D58F / #EFD3A0 / #F2CF96) distinct from error; mark-06 and marks-b/system.png tint the needs-you glyph in error red; anim-05-status says 'if the owner keeps error red for attention, the marker is red and the ladder argument in color/ does not apply here'.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: attention = lit accent (new token, monochrome-safe ladder) or attention = error (today).

conflicts.what: The tray's attention cue and small drawing: marks-a and anim-04 keep today's composition (the raven slides to the 50x42 box plus the 18 px badge, plus a ring) with the -16 head as the drawing; marks-b makes mark-05-glyph the tinted tray shape and swaps in mark-06-flight-small as the attention shape ('replaces or sits beside the perched tray raven'); the colour dimension shows 'the raven itself' tinted at 45/75/100 % plus the badge. Shape change vs badge vs tint-only, with three different small drawings (head, glyph tile, m16 pixel).
conflicts.decisionNeeded: Which small drawing lives in the tray, notification and favicon, and whether attention is a badge, a tint step, a shape swap or a combination.

conflicts.what: Alphabet policy: type-system.md rules 'no triangle-arrow, no braille, no runes in terminal art (they would come from a system fallback font and not match the cell)' and 'terminal art uses the three blocks and the light box set as its safe core'; the ascii dimension recommends braille for README/docs and ships braille portraits, mark-04 ships ascii-braille.txt for README/docs/tmux, anim-04-boot's rain is braille, ascii-03's one-row glyph and its c-variant use geometric shapes. The rule and the artefacts contradict unless the rule is scoped to the apps' terminal view.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: Where braille and geometric shapes are allowed (README, docs, kitty-class terminals, Termux) and where only blocks and light box drawing are (apps' terminal view, status bars, installer console).

conflicts.what: The README hero: ascii-04 calls lockup-d 'the direct replacement for today's SVG + figlet hero' (text in a code block, ANSI Shadow kept); type-system says 'the wordmark in a README is the SVG, not live text and not pre art' and word-01 says the double-line shadow set 'is being retired'; anim-01 offers an animated SVG in img; anim-04-boot a hero GIF; mark-06 'the splash lockup or the inverse left of the wordmark'; word-10 its geometry SVG. Five incompatible heroes.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: Image (static lockup SVG, animated SVG, GIF) or text block, and which one; and whether ANSI Shadow survives anywhere.

conflicts.what: The 80-column server-side splash and attach banner: ascii-04 lockup-a (5-line raven + ANSI Shadow) vs the wordmark verdict's word-10-perch / word-09 hairline 'as the signature banner, printed server-side: huginn-status, the attach banner' vs the block family (word-02/03). Two dimensions each name a different letterform family for the same line of output.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: One terminal letterform family (hairline, block, or figlet) for server banners; the other files become references.

conflicts.what: The client's 7-bit raven and help header (huginn.sh:988): ascii-03 raven-4line-ascii-a (12 cols, (o)=- head, one = fewer than today) composed into ascii-04 help-header-ascii; word-09/word-10 ascii.txt as 'the CLI client's help masthead' (5 rows, hatched # bird); mark-04 ascii-7bit.txt (8 rows); while anim-02's 7-bit landing 'ends on exactly' today's (o)==- raven and anim-04-boot's 7-bit boot assembles 'the client's own help-screen raven (o)==-' unchanged.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: Which 7-bit raven is the client's (and whether the help raven changes), then rebuild the anim-ascii twins on it.

conflicts.what: Canonical source of the mark: marks-a, mark-05, mark-06 and the ascii regen pipeline assume an SVG path ('swap is one edit'; regen.sh takes an SVG); mark-04 says 'raven.svg would be replaced by grid.txt as the canonical source' and forbids anti-aliasing and non-integer scales, which the blink lid, the glyph scatter, the new flight geometry and anim-04's anti-aliased ring and 300 ms sub-integer slide all rely on. mark-04 ships its own blink and call frames instead.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: If the pixel mark wins, accept that anim-vector is largely redone from the grid; if a smooth mark wins, accept mark-04's terminal art is a derivative, not the source.

conflicts.what: mark-02 says 'hard edges want some geometry in the surrounding type and icon system or they date next to soft Material 3 surfaces'; the apps' house rules are Material 3 with 8/10/6/20 dp radii and mark-03 is built with round caps and joins as the icon-set companion. No geometric icon set or sharper radius system was explored.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: Whether choosing mark-02 commits the apps to a sharper icon/radius system (not in this round) or the mark is used only outside the apps.

conflicts.what: Tile corner radius: marks-b tiles use 'the set's 22.5 % corner radius' (rx 12/54, 18/80, 36/160); marks-a tiles reuse raven-tile.svg's radius without stating it; the apps' most common radius is 8 dp.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: One tile radius for launcher, taskbar and .ico masters.

conflicts.what: The cursor device: word-03/08 specify 'one column, full block height, full block in Unicode files and | in ASCII files'; anim-04-boot types the banner 'behind a left-half-block cursor' (and _ in 7-bit); anim-05 (c) is a block 0.55 x line height breathing on PulseDot; type-02 puts the raven where the cursor would be.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: One cursor glyph, proportion and rhythm for terminal art and the apps.

conflicts.what: Light-scheme tokens: color-01 darkens the light primary from #7A5A16 to #6B4E10 and moves onSurfaceVariant from #8A8177 to #A39A8F (keeping #8A8177 as stateIdle); type-system.md and all three specimens pin #7A5A16 (5.95:1) and 'muted #8A8177 for labelSmall... do not go lighter on the ground or darker on the text'.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: Adopt color-01's values and re-render the type specimens, or keep today's two values and let color-01 re-solve its idle/working 12 L* rule.

conflicts.what: marks-a previews render the tray composition in #7B8794, 'tray grey', the Electron colour the brief lists as an incoherence and the colour dimension replaces with stateIdle or the 45 % monochrome tint; marks-b/system.png uses the apps' state language. Previews, not decisions, but the marks-a sheets show the retired colour.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: None beyond re-rendering marks-a tray cells in the chosen state tints before the brand book.

conflicts.what: Motion energy: the brief's house rule is 'a slow pulse rather than a spinner'; anim-ascii anim-01 (a) is a 2 Hz wingbeat 'faster than that on purpose' and anim-05 changes the tmux segment every second; anim-vector keeps everything on the PulseDot clock or plays once.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: Whether the CLI and tmux may be livelier than the apps (with the 4 fps and breathe options as the calm defaults) or the house rule applies everywhere.

conflicts.what: Naming: anim-ascii and anim-vector both number their variations anim-01..anim-05 (brief rule 7 asks for dimension-nn-slug), so ids are unique only by slug and the two anim-01 / anim-05 pairs are easy to confuse in a brand book.
conflicts.decisionNeeded: Rename one dimension's ids (e.g. tanim-nn / vanim-nn) before the brand book references them.

duplicates.note: Three renderings of one idea - terminal glyphs assembling into the raven: a vector scatter for docs/splash, braille rain frames for the terminal, and a mark whose icon IS the glyphs. Pick one as the brand's assembly motif.

The same four-cell one-row glyph, intentionally sourced from ascii-03 (color: 'two dimensions must not ship two ravens for one line'); only word-11-oneline and mark-04's (o)> suggestion break the single source (see conflicts).
Four state-glyph tables for the tab title and status bar, three of them slightly different.
Three implementations of the tmux status-left segment (ascii-04 snippet with a needs-you condition, color tmux.conf.snippet per direction, anim-05 1 fps frames) with two different colour rules.
Four blinks: vector lid, terminal frames, pixel blink frames (SVG and text), and the glyph's eye-cell blink (claim only).

Four unrelated flying-raven drawings: from below (mark-06), side-view new geometry (anim-03's flyer), quadrant flying poses (anim-02), and the 3-cell wingbeat from behind (anim-01 a). None share a silhouette.
Two different 24-column terminal ravens: ascii-02's hand-redrawn 24x8 half-block (used by ascii-04 lockup-c/d) and anim-03's sampled 24x15 quadrant bitmap (used by anim-04-boot).
Three head-only small marks for the same 16 px slot: the two -16 head drawings are near-identical in marks-a/compare.png row 4, and mark-05 is a third head in a tile.
Five 7-bit help/CLI ravens: raven-4line-ascii-a/b and its help-header composition, today's (o)==- as kept by anim-02 and anim-04-boot, and mark-04's 8- and 16-row ascii-7bit files.
Two narrow 3-row marks for one slot; acknowledged, word-06 chosen because it cannot tofu.
Two 7-bit capital marks; acknowledged, word-07 dropped from the verdict so the hairline family's ascii.txt keeps one letterform.
Four braille ravens for README/docs at 48, 24, 16 and 28 columns, from three different source drawings.
Five cursor devices with three glyphs (full block column, left-half block, breathing block) and one raven-as-cursor.
The per-direction terminal READMEs are generated copies of the shared layer with the direction's numbers; intentional.

marks-a.why: Path-data drop-in that 'reads as a raven from 32 px up' with a genuine 16 px head drawing and the launcher safe circle held; the lowest-risk way to fix the 'blob body, stick tail' complaint.

Same box and transform, visibly sharper at 64/32, and the only smooth mark whose morph (unfold) and terminal tracing (braille) ship as files; 12 vertices port to Compose, AVD and ASCII without curve questions.
Not a primary candidate by its own README, but the right companion for in-app icon rows and currentColor tinting beside Lucide-weight icons.

marks-b.why: The only direction where 'the tray icon, the terminal banner and the CLI help raven are literally the same cells' and the only one with a CLI-safe 7-bit form; answers the ASCII ask structurally.
The best 16 px tray shape in the set by marks-b's own ranking and 'the best single image' (the inverse); tinted-by-state with no badge needed.
The hero and splash companion that says raven most specifically and carries the fly-out-and-return story; never the primary.

ascii.why: The working set every other dimension already consumes: the one-row glyph, the help raven drop-in, the 2/3/5-line ravens, each client-facing size with a 7-bit twin.
The splash/README size that 'reads as the raven at a 16px cell' in 8 rows, with the GitHub line-height case tested.
The help-header heredoc drop-in, the ASCII banner and the tmux segment are the concrete CLI deliverables, once the gold rule is aligned with colour.

wordmark.why: type-system.md's verdict: holds at 24 px, one family for the UI, and the only direction with outlined SVGs for README and installer.
The one terminal wordmark with the raven in it, in three charsets plus a geometry SVG, so the same lockup reaches server banners, the 7-bit client and the README.
The only one-row mark 'identical in every font and every terminal', with title-state variants; the fallback the one-row conflict resolves to if font coverage wins.

anim-ascii.why: Gives connected and detached a brand verb with 7-bit twins that can go into huginn.sh today and end on the help raven.
1-fps-safe tmux segment carrying all three states with the state-to-frame-to-colour table that cross-references colour.
The README hero GIF and first-run splash under 2 s, with a measured bash player and a 7-bit boot small enough to inline.

anim-vector.why: Option (c) reads at 16 px, adds no geometry and shares the apps' PulseDot clock, which is the cohesion the owner asked for.
Starts and ends on frames TrayIcons.kt already draws; the Kotlin spec and generated frame tables make it the most implementable piece in the folder.
Zero new geometry, resting state is the mark, GIF and AVD fallbacks shipped; the safe hero/idle motion for any smooth mark.

color.why: The dimension's own recommendation: zero drift, fixes every incoherence in the brief (tray colours, demo theme, mute CLI, missing tiers) with the migration list written.
If the overhaul must be seen in colour: the cleanest terminal semantics (accent and warning in different hues) and the best raven story.
The most dramatic; viable only if the owner accepts the named collision with the host product's terracotta and orange-as-warning on notification surfaces.

bundles.name: Quiet evolution
bundles.mark: mark-01-refined (mark-02-faceted is the swappable sharper twin: same 108 box, translate and winding)
bundles.smallMark: mark-01-refined-16 head for tray 16-22 px and favicon-16; mark-01-refined-status for ic_stat at 48/72
bundles.heroMark: mark-01-refined / -tile / -inverse at 512; installer and README via type-01 lockup.svg and lockup-dark.svg re-cut with the mark-01 path
bundles.terminalRaven: ascii-02 raven-24-half for the splash, ascii-03 set (one-row glyph for tmux, raven-4line-ascii-a + ascii-04 help-header-ascii for the client, 5-line beside the wordmark), all regenerated from mark-01 with ascii/regen.sh and the src/ grids re-tuned
bundles.wordmarkTerminal: word-10-perch (rounded, square, ascii; bird re-rasterised from mark-01) with word-09-hairline where no bird fits and word-06-pagga under 34 columns; one-row: ascii-03's glyph with (o)=- in the client
bundles.stateGlyphs: The colour dimension's table: filled circle / diamond / hollow circle / small hollow circle, ASCII * ! o - in the clients; tray and apps draw dots tinted stateIdle / stateWorking / stateAttention + badge
bundles.rationale: Every piece is a path-data swap, a rename or a regeneration: marks-a 'drop-in in box, transform, winding and eye-as-hole rule', color-01 'zero brand drift', anim-vector 'the swap is one edit', type-01 ships outlined SVGs, ascii has regen.sh. The newness is where the brief wanted it: raven anatomy, a drawn wordmark, a terminal signature and motion. The type-system verdict defends the hairline-next-to-800-sans pairing ('the type's job is to be quiet'), and the one-row glyph is the one three dimensions already share.
bundles.risk: color-01 is 'the least new' and mark-01 vs today is subtle at icon size; two hand redraws (word-10's bird, anim-03's flyer if used) and the ascii src/ grids do not regenerate automatically; the geometric-shape one-row glyph falls to a fallback font inside the apps' JetBrains Mono terminal view (type-system.md), so the in-app line may need the block fallback or (o>.

bundles.name: Terminal-native
bundles.mark: mark-04-pixel (grid.txt becomes the canonical source; generate.sh calls grid2svg.py / grid2png.py)
bundles.smallMark: m16 native at 16 and 32 (tray, favicon, .ico), png/tray-20 and -24 padded for 125/150 % trays, adaptive-fg PNGs for Android; m16 1x+pad for the 24 dp status icon
bundles.heroMark: m32 at integer multiples (8x = 256) and mark-04-pixel-inverse-32: 'chunky by design', the honest look of the direction; the 54-cell tile for the launcher
bundles.terminalRaven: mark-04's own files: ascii-halfblock (tmux, huginn-status, apps' terminal view at line-height 1.0), ascii-braille (README and docs), ascii-7bit and ascii-7bit-32 (CLI help and banner), ascii-halfblock-small for tight spaces
bundles.wordmarkTerminal: The block-only family that word-06 says 'pairs with word-02/word-03 in a block-only system': word-03-mono9-lower with the cursor for the attach banner, word-02-mono9-caps rendered to an image for the README, word-06-pagga under 34 columns; one-row: word-11-oneline (o> everywhere, since mark-04 ships no one-row glyph and Plex Mono lacks the geometric shapes
bundles.typeDirection: type-02-plex-mono (word-03 and word-08 are 'this direction's terminal twins'; Plex Mono has blocks 32/32 and box 128/128 so the block marks render inside the apps)
bundles.stateGlyphs: ASCII * ! o - on every terminal surface (Plex Mono has 1/96 geometric shapes, so no circle or diamond glyphs); the apps draw dots in stateIdle / stateWorking / stateAttention; mark-04's blink and call frames are the in-tray and in-terminal idle/speaking motion
bundles.rationale: marks-b: 'the pixel raven is the only one that makes the terminal art and the icon the same drawing, and the only one with a CLI-safe form'. Block-only wordmarks, a mono with full block coverage, 7-bit state glyphs and (o> mean nothing can tofu on any platform, which is the owner's ASCII ask taken literally. color-02 gives the terminal its cleanest semantics (accent in cyan, warning in yellow, 128 degrees apart) and makes the overhaul visible in colour, matching a direction whose icon already looks new.
bundles.risk: mark-04's integer rule: ragged or small at 20/24 px trays and never exact at 48/256 tiles with a 10 % inset; 'retro' above 64 px; type-02 'pulls the other way' from Theme.kt's 'terminal that does not look like a terminal emulator' and its tittle lockup fails; color-02 regenerates every raster and 'borders on the dark-dev-tool convention'; the anim-vector set (blink lid, scatter, ring, sub-integer slide) does not port to a crisp-edge grid, so anim-01/02/03/04 are dropped; the 7-bit anim-ascii twins must be rebuilt on the pixel raven; the tray PNGs are bone-only and need regenerating per state tint.

bundles.name: Story-led (marks-b system)
bundles.mark: mark-05-glyph (the tile with the raven as negative space) as the screen mark: tray, notification, favicon tinted by state; -tile from 48 px up for launcher and taskbar; -window for docs and CLI chrome
bundles.smallMark: mark-05-glyph primary untiled at 16/32 tinted stateIdle / stateWorking; mark-06-flight-small tinted stateAttention as the needs-you shape (marks-b: 'the tray's attention state')
bundles.heroMark: mark-06-flight-splash and -inverse for README hero, launch screen and installer welcome panel ('the hero and launch moment'), with mark-05-glyph-inverse as the secondary big image
bundles.terminalRaven: As marks-b/system.png composes it: mark-04-pixel's braille in README and docs, 7-bit in the CLI clients, half-block in tmux ('the pixel raven is the terminal'); the glyph's window form as docs chrome
bundles.wordmarkTerminal: word-09-hairline (rounded, square, ascii) composed beside the pixel raven with ascii/lockup.py (composite not yet rendered); one-row: ascii-03's glyph with (o)=- in the client
bundles.typeDirection: type-01-schibsted for UI and the wordmark; type-03-instrument only as a display-size alternative for README, installer and About if the carved voice is wanted (its README: 'The serif never appears below 28 px')
bundles.stateGlyphs: The colour dimension's table (filled circle / diamond / hollow circle, ASCII * ! o -) with attention in the cream-amber #F2CF96 and the flight-small glyph as the tray's attention shape; the glyph's eye cell is the cursor-blink idle (claimed by mark-05, not built)
bundles.rationale: This is marks-b's own 'How they fit together': glyph = tray/notification/favicon shape tinted by state, flight-small = attention, flight = hero and launch, pixel = terminal; system.png shows the combination on the app ground with the state language. color-03 is the dimension's dramatic option, 'the raven's eye in firelight', which matches a hero that is a raven in flight rather than a perched icon. It is the bundle a reviewer sees as new from across the room.
bundles.risk: There is no single primary drawing: mark-05 'is a head, not a whole raven... it needs the full mark (or mark-06-flight) beside it', so three drawings (glyph, flight, pixel) share the identity and species certainty differs between them; color-03's 'the ember is Claude's colour' and 'orange is a warning colour in every OS' on the very notification and permission surfaces the product lives on (its README says it is less suited there); none of the anim-vector pieces built on the perched raven.svg transfer to the glyph (anim-02's scatter and anim-04's slide must be rebuilt, anim-01/03 do not apply), and the flight-small swap in the tray is not animated; the hairline-plus-pixel lockup is a claim until composed.

decisionChecklist.decision: Attention semantics and what the accent means: attention = the accent lit up (new stateAttention token) or attention = error (today); accent = working (color, anim-05) or accent = needs-you (ascii-04's tmux mock).
decisionChecklist.note: First because the tray, tmux, title glyphs and the state table all hang on it; every later pick inherits the answer.

decisionChecklist.decision: Palette ground: finish the current palette, or depart cool or hot.
decisionChecklist.note: Decides whether tiles, .ico, wizard.bmp and README SVGs regenerate (02/03) and whether the gold survives in the lockups; the terminal layer and state ladder carry over regardless.

decisionChecklist.decision: Primary mark family: marks-a path swap (01 or 02), the pixel grid (04), or the glyph-plus-flight system (05/06).
decisionChecklist.note: Also decides the canonical source (SVG path vs grid.txt) and therefore how much of anim-vector and the ascii regen survive (conflict on canonical source).

decisionChecklist.decision: The small-size answer for tray, favicon-16 and notification, and the attention cue there.
decisionChecklist.note: -16 head vs m16 pixel vs glyph tile; badge + ring vs flight-small shape vs tint-only; marks-b ranks the tray candidates glyph > pixel m16 > flight-small.

decisionChecklist.decision: The hero form for README, splash and installer.
decisionChecklist.note: Image (static lockup SVG, animated SVG, GIF) or text block; animated SVG in img ignores reduced motion in Chromium, so the README may need poster.png plus a link.
type-system.md's verdict is type-01 with seven static TTFs (~0.75 MB); type-02 only with a block-only terminal family; type-03 only above 28 px.

decisionChecklist.decision: The terminal letterform family and the fate of ANSI Shadow.
decisionChecklist.note: Hairline (wordmark verdict) vs block (pairs with pixel art) vs keeping figlet for the 80-column splash (ascii-04 lockup-a/d); word-06 is the narrow fallback in either case.

decisionChecklist.decision: The one-row raven for tmux, the first line and titles, Unicode and 7-bit.
decisionChecklist.note: The four-cell glyph is shared by four dimensions but is absent from JetBrains Mono and Plex Mono; (o> is 7-bit and font-proof but 'a generic bird'; (o)=- vs (o)==- for the client must also be settled.

decisionChecklist.decision: The client's 7-bit raven and help header, then rebuild the anim-ascii 7-bit twins on it.
decisionChecklist.note: ascii-04 help-header-ascii is the only ready heredoc drop-in; anim-02 and anim-04-boot currently end on today's raven.

decisionChecklist.decision: One state-glyph table for tab titles, huginn-status, Telegram and the clients.
decisionChecklist.note: Triangle vs diamond for attention, o vs - for waiting; colour owns the semantic set, the others adopt and huginn-claude-title's defaults change.

decisionChecklist.decision: Alphabet policy: where braille and geometric shapes are allowed and where only blocks and the light box set are.
decisionChecklist.note: type-system.md's rule as written forbids files the ascii and anim dimensions recommend; scope it (apps' terminal view and status bars vs README, docs, kitty-class terminals).

decisionChecklist.decision: Motion set and energy: which of the ten animations ship, whether the CLI may beat at 2 Hz, and whether the chat indicator keeps PulseDot's breath.
decisionChecklist.note: anim-vector obeys the house rule; anim-ascii names its calm options (4 fps, breathe); the tray plays anim-04 once at 10 fps.

decisionChecklist.decision: Cursor device: glyph, proportion and rhythm.
decisionChecklist.note: Full block column vs left-half block vs breathing block vs raven-as-cursor; small, but it appears on five surfaces.

decisionChecklist.decision: Tile radius and whether a faceted mark commits the apps to sharper geometry.

verdictOnRound: The set is sufficient to decide the three load-bearing choices (mark family, palette, type direction) and most terminal pieces: every variation is honest about its limits, the marks were revised to real 16 px answers, and colour, wordmark and both animation dimensions each end in a defensible recommendation. Two things need a second round before the brand book: a cross-dimension composite round in which the ascii art, the wordmark lockups, the anim-vector files and the colour sheets are rebuilt on each candidate mark (one sheet per bundle), because today only marks-b/system.png shows a candidate mark in context; and a reconciliation pass owned by the colour dimension that issues one state/attention/one-row-glyph table and re-cuts ascii-04's tmux snippet and word-11's title states to it. A verification pass on Windows (PowerShell player, cli-colors.ps1, conhost) and Termux should precede any CLI promise in the book; marks-a vs marks-b, type and palette can be decided now.
